about: The gospel of the Fourth Sunday of Advent. Luke dates the year by seven offices at once — an emperor, a governor, three tetrarchs and two high priests — and only then says the word of God came to a man who holds none of them.

seg.tr: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate governed Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of Iturea and the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene, under the high priests Annas and Caiaphas, the word of the Lord came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the desert.

ex.w006: The phrase “procuránte Póntio Piláto” sets the time of the events: “when Pontius Pilate governed Judea”.

seg.tr: He went throughout the whole region of the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, as it is written in the book of the sayings of the prophet Isaiah: A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight. Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill brought low; the crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth. And all flesh will see the salvation of God.

ex.w059: Here the noun, a book, and not the adjective that shares its spelling.
